question: Why does Bryson say we are lucky to exist at all?
answer: Because our existence depends on a long chain of improbable events: a planet at the right distance from a stable star, a large moon steadying its tilt, a Jupiter shielding it from comets, and an unbroken line of ancestors, each surviving long enough to reproduce, for nearly four billion years.
move: Every survivor stands at the end of a long line of lucky breaks.
simply: For you to be here, every ancestor, back to the first tiny creatures, had to survive long enough to have children. Not one link could break.
why: It's a humbling frame for daily worries, and a reminder that improbable chains happen all the time when you look back from the end.
